# Provider matrix

Every collection source declares the same contract: capabilities, terms, data
classification, required secrets, timeout, rate limit, cost unit, cache policy, and
fixture support. An adapter whose secrets are absent stays in the catalog and reports
`unconfigured`; its checks resolve to `unknown`/`unavailable` and never to a pass or a
failure.

The core demo runs on the keyless adapters alone — no paid provider key is required to
collect DNS, e-mail policy, TLS/certificate, HTTP header, RDAP, and Certificate
Transparency evidence.

## Terms and licensing notes

### `certificate_transparency` — Certificate Transparency asset candidate collector

Certificate Transparency logs are public append-only records (RFC 6962). Names observed here are candidates, not confirmed organizational assets.

Reference: <https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6962>

### `dns_resilience` — Domain and DNS resilience collector

Public DNS data obtained through the configured recursive resolver.

### `email_trust` — E-mail trust collector

Public DNS policy records and the published MTA-STS policy file.

### `http_surface` — Web surface collector

Single unauthenticated GET of the public site root over each scheme.

### `passive_asset_intelligence` — Passive asset intelligence provider (opt-in)

Licensed passive dataset. Redistribution of raw records is prohibited; only a normalized subset plus a content hash is retained.

Licensing: Requires a provider agreement before enablement.

### `rdap_registration` — RDAP registration collector

RDAP is a public registration data protocol; responses may redact contacts under registry policy and GDPR. Contact objects are never stored.

Reference: <https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7483>

### `reputation_otx` — Open Threat Exchange indicators (opt-in)

Community-contributed indicators, which means variable quality and real false positives. Results are private-report-only and must never reach a public page or an opt-in publication: publishing 'this town hall appears in threat intelligence' on evidence that can be wrong is the sharpest reputational risk in this product. The policy catalogue enforces it -- the reputation check is classed `private_only`, which the publication projector filters on.

Reference: <https://otx.alienvault.com/>

Licensing: Free API key; terms not independently verified.

### `reputation_safe_browsing` — Reputation and safe-browsing provider (opt-in)

Official reputation API. A listing is a third-party signal, never evidence of compromise; disagreement between providers is preserved.

Licensing: Requires a provider agreement before enablement.

### `reputation_spamhaus_dqs` — Spamhaus Data Query Service (opt-in)

Free Data Query Service is limited to non-commercial use and must not consistently exceed 100,000 queries per day. Spamhaus's published terms do not address using results inside a tool offered to other organisations, or displaying them to those organisations -- which is what this platform would do. Silence is not permission: enablement waits on a written answer from Spamhaus.

Reference: <https://www.spamhaus.com/terms-of-use-fair-use-policy-for-free-data-query-service/>

Licensing: Blocked on written confirmation that the free tier covers this use.

### `tls_certificate` — TLS and certificate collector

Direct TLS handshakes against the authorized host; no data is sent.

## Keyless coverage

6 of 10 adapters require no secret. They cover all 10 core capabilities:

- `ct.asset_candidates`
- `dns.caa`
- `dns.delegation`
- `dns.dnssec`
- `email.dmarc`
- `email.mta_sts`
- `email.spf`
- `http.headers`
- `rdap.registration`
- `tls.certificate`

## Reading this table

- **Secrets** — environment variable names only. Values never appear in the repository.
- **Rate limit** — requests per second with burst; a `min-interval` entry additionally
  spaces consecutive calls.
- **Cache** — time-to-live in seconds. A cache is only enabled where provider terms
  permit storage.
- **Classification** — `public_observation` may inform the public projection;
  `tenant_confidential` and `restricted_provider_data` never leave the private workspace.

## Degradation

| Situation | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Adapter secret absent | Adapter reports `unconfigured`; dependent checks are `unknown` |
| Provider rate limit reached | Call refused with `rate_limited`; quota is not consumed |
| Provider quota exhausted | Call refused with `quota_exhausted` and shown on the quota dashboard |
| Repeated provider errors | Circuit opens; calls refused with `circuit_open` until it resets |
| Providers disagree | Every claim is retained and the subject is marked contested |
